name: vault-browse-allaway-empty
comment: Vault Browse face execution plan, Slice 9 (empty states): the 'everything here is away' cause is DISTINCT from Slice 6's own away fixture (tests/fixtures/vault/browse-states-away-seed) - that fixture has durable index rows for its away root, so VaultBrowseAway::offlineBrowseAt() correctly keeps its tiles VISIBLE, marked away (design §4.7 'nothing disappears' - proven by vault_browse_away.json, grid count 2, not this cause at all). THIS fixture is the other real case the design's four causes distinguish: a confirmed root whose drive is away AND was never scanned while present (config.json declares a root at a path that has never existed on this machine, no index-v1.sqlite seeded at all - zero durable rows, mirroring the C++ unit proof tst_vault_browse_away.cpp::offlineBrowseAtIsEmptyWithoutPriorPublishedRows) - there is nothing to fall back to, so the grid is legitimately empty AND the reason is away-ness, not a genuinely empty folder. Run with --seed tests/fixtures/vault/browse-allaway-empty-seed (absolute path).

steps.label: the session answers, drive gated on
one visible window, isolated data root
the boot splash has left the screen
open the Vault via the folder door
the browse face renders (a confirmed root exists, even though it is away)
the rail marks the root unavailable
the grid settles at zero - nothing was ever recorded for this away root
the empty-cause component reports allAway with the mock's exact copy

expect.value: Everything here lives on a drive that is not connected. Nothing has been forgotten.
